:::{#exm-random-variable}
#### Number of heads in two coin flips

<!-- no-figure: the four-outcome sample space is listed in full below -->

Flip a fair coin twice.
The sample space is $\samplespace = \set{HH, HT, TH, TT}$,
each outcome with probability $1/4$.
Let $\Rvar_1$ equal $1$ if the first flip lands heads and $0$ otherwise,
and let $\Rvar_2$ be the same for the second flip.
Let $\Sumsym = \Rvar_1 + \Rvar_2$ be the number of heads:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Sumsym(HH) &= 2, \\
\Sumsym(HT) &= 1, \\
\Sumsym(TH) &= 1, \\
\Sumsym(TT) &= 0
\end{aligned}
$$

Then $\{\Sumsym = 1\} = \set{HT, TH}$, so

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Pr(\Sumsym = 1) &= 1/4 + 1/4 \\
&= 1/2.
\end{aligned}
$$

:::
